summary: The bill creates a federal entitlement program that pays states, territories, and tribes most of the cost of providing free or low-cost high-quality child care to every child under age 6, using cost-based provider rates, quality tiers, sliding-scale copays, and grants to expand supply and extend Head Start and preschool hours.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new federal entitlement-style child care program with open-ended appropriations ('such sums as may be necessary' for FY2026–2031) plus $20B+ in specific grants and $9B annual BASE grants. This directly and substantially expands federal outlays on child care services, provider supports, and administration.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures.
The bill addresses child care and early learning only; it does not modify health insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, or medical service delivery.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions address immigration status, visas, border enforcement, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect defense budgets, military personnel, or national security spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, emissions, or conservation programs.

The bill establishes sliding-scale child care subsidies, guaranteed access for low-income and vulnerable families, and direct payments to providers serving SNAP/TANF/WIC-eligible children. This constitutes a major expansion of means-tested family support analogous to existing welfare programs.

The legislation creates a universal birth-to-five child care and preschool entitlement, funds quality improvement systems, teacher credentials, and mixed-delivery early education programs with strong federal standards and oversight—directly increasing federal investment and involvement in public early childhood education.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-use treatment policy.
No provisions alter sentencing, policing, or criminal justice procedures.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill authorizes large new mandatory and discretionary spending without offsetting revenue, thereby accepting increased deficit spending to finance the new programs.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill requires wage ladders and living wages for child care staff but contains no explicit provisions expanding or restricting union rights or collective bargaining.

The bill permits certificates to be used at sectarian providers as indirect assistance and applies standard nondiscrimination rules; it does not create new religious exemptions or alter civil-rights enforcement.
